brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: Base structure, bolted into one body
requirements.evidence: There are three bases in a row: full bases at (-1,0) and (0,0), and a west-half base at (1,0). They are joined by joint bolts jointBolt:0#-1,0#0 and jointBolt:0#0,0#0. check_build shows no errors and meshClash reads "clear".

There are two 3-compartment bins (hex-bin-full-div3), at (-1,0) and (0,0). They drop in and hang on their rims, with no fixings. The bin at (-1,0) is open at the top. The bin at (0,0) sits under the cover that holds the handle, so you get to it from above only by taking that cover off.
drawer:0#1,0#cut is a slide drawer on the cut face of the half base at (1,0). The configurator offered it there and placed it.

handle:0,0,0;top sits on a full top cover (cover:0,0,0;full;top) over the middle cell, held by three inserts. That puts it centred over the row for carrying. This is a fit check only; no load rating is claimed.

The build is compact: 3 cells, one level, one body, with the handle in the middle. But the 10 open side faces have no caps (check_build lists them as info only), and nothing holds the bins in while it's being carried.

finish.summary: This is a one-level, 3-cell organizer: two full bases, each with a 3-compartment removable bin, and a half base at the east end with a slide drawer on its cut face. A carry handle sits on a top cover over the middle cell. Everything is bolted into one body, check_build shows no errors and the mesh check is clear. One trade-off: the configurator only offers a handle on a full top cover. A half cover over the drawer cell got no handle offer, so the handle went over the middle bin, and you reach that bin from above only by taking its cover off. Side caps were not added.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
